new.title: RR Lyrae stars as distance indicators I. Sample selection and characterisation
new.summary: RR Lyrae stars (RRL) are well-established Population II distance indicators, with period-metallicity-luminosity (PLZ) relations linking pulsational properties to absolute luminosity. Gaia parallaxes now allow these relations to be anchored to geometric distances with unprecedented precision, offering an independent route to the extragalactic distance scale. We present the first paper in a series aimed at deriving new empirical PLZ and metallicity-luminosity relations for RRL in the optical and near-infrared. We describe the selection and characterisation of a sample of bright nearby field RRL, with distances anchored to reliable Gaia DR3 parallaxes. We conducted a multi-band photometric campaign of 172 RRL: 101 in Johnson-Cousins UBVRI with the IAC80 telescope and 130 in JHKs with the IRSF telescope, with 59 stars in common. The iron abundances come from the Spectroscopic Rome RRL Catalog catalogue, mostly from high-resolution spectroscopy. The light curves were modelled with GLOESS (optical) and near-infrared templates, and the mean magnitudes, amplitudes, and Fourier parameters were derived via a bootstrap Monte Carlo method. The linear relations were fitted with a Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo method. The sample spans -3.4 to 0.2 dex in [Fe/H]. We found tight relations between the Fourier parameter $\phi_{31}$ in each optical and Gaia band and its V-band value for RRab stars (scatter below 0.06). The near-infrared amplitude ratios with respect to V or G increase continuously with period, without the break reported in globular clusters. We provide a homogeneous calibration of the colour at minimum light across all filter combinations from U-B to H-Ks, revealing significant period and metallicity dependences, and we use it to derive reddening estimates for 15 stars outside current 3D extinction maps.

new.title: Evidence for an Evolving Surface on the Partly Burnt Runaway Stellar Remnant GD 492
new.summary: GD 492 (LP 40-365) is a partly burnt, hypervelocity runaway stellar remnant thought to have survived a thermonuclear supernova. We analyze 12 sectors of TESS photometry spanning more than four years to investigate the previously reported 8.9-hr photometric modulation of the star. We find that the modulation changes with time, with individual-sector fits yielding apparent periods ranging from 8.8606 to 8.9048 hr (0.5% changes), more than 25 times the formal measurement uncertainties. Both the period and shape of the modulation evolve on a timescales of approximately one to two months. We show qualitatively that a two-spot model with evolving surface structure can reproduce several of the observed light-curve morphologies, although the geometry of the spots is not uniquely constrained. These observations suggest that changing surface inhomogeneities are a plausible origin of the photometric variability. Differential rotation and magnetic activity may contribute to this evolution, potentially providing new constraints on the outer convective structure of GD 492 and on the interpretation of its atmospheric abundances.

new.title: Transport of High Energy Protons from CME-Shock to the Sun and its Connection to Extended Gamma-rays Observed by FERMI
new.summary: This work is motivated by the Large Area Telescope (LAT) observations of long-duration gamma rays from flares associated often with fast Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs), several of which originate behind the limb (BTL) of the Sun. Our aim is to test the feasibility of the scenario whereby the gamma-rays are produced by CME-shock accelerated particles escaping from downstream to the Sun by investigating the transport of protons in this process for the flare of 2014 September 1. We use results from the global MHD modeling by the Alfvén Wave Solar Model (AWSoM) to obtain the characteristics of downstream plasma, such as magnetic field geometry, Alfvén speed, and energy density of turbulence. This allows us to evaluate the variations of the proton scattering mean free path with energy and distance from the CME-shock. Using an approximate analytic relation between the relevant time scales of the transport, we determine the energy dependence of the residence time at (or escape time from) different distances above the photosphere, and determine the evolution of the proton spectrum from the acceleration site to the photosphere. These results can be used to obtain the spectrum of the observed gamma-rays. Inversely, because of insignificant energy loss or gain during transport, this is a reversible process and the spectrum of protons at the photosphere, obtained from the observed gamma-rays, can be ``de-evolved" back to the CME using the same algorithm. Comparison of these spectra with the in situ observations of Solar Energetic Particles (SEPs) could then shed light on their transport from the CME to the Earth.

new.title: Binary mass transfer fossil in the ancient GD-1 stellar stream
new.summary: We report the discovery of J0930+2902, the first carbon-enhanced metal-poor star with s-process enrichment (CEMP-s) identified in the GD-1 stellar stream, which is widely believed to originate from the tidal disruption of an old, metal-poor globular cluster. Using high-resolution Subaru/HDS spectroscopy, we present a comprehensive chemical abundance analysis of this star. Stellar atmospheric parameters were re-derived using Gaia photometry and parallaxes, combined with an iterative non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) analysis of Fe lines. We determine abundances for 22 elements, including NLTE analyses of C, Na, Mg, Ca, Ti, Cr, Mn, Co, Sr, Y, Zr, Ba, and Eu. J0930+2902 exhibits pronounced enhancements of C, N, Na, and s-process elements, together with a low $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 7.4, consistent with enrichment through binary mass transfer from a former asymptotic giant branch (AGB) companion. Large radial-velocity variations and a significant near-ultraviolet excess independently indicate the presence of a white dwarf companion, providing strong support for this scenario. Comparisons with FRUITY AGB nucleosynthesis models show that the residual neutron-capture abundance pattern is best reproduced by a low-mass AGB companion with an initial mass of approximately 3.0 $M_{\odot}$. Its enhancements of C, N, Na, and s-process elements make it chemically distinct from the other confirmed GD-1 members. These results identify J0930+2902 as a fossil record of binary mass transfer preserved in the ancient GD-1 stellar stream, demonstrating that binary interaction can leave long-lived chemical signatures in accreted stellar populations.

new.title: A magneto-convective origin for solar-wind Alfvenic fluctuations
new.summary: The solar wind is a highly structured and supersonic plasma outflow that originates in the Sun's outer atmosphere. The energy source driving the wind is still subject to intense debate. Recent observations point to magnetic reconnection as a primary driver, while Alfvenic waves launched by surface convection are often invoked as a key contributor. Whether fluctuations in the young solar wind originate in convectively driven waves has not been tested observationally. Here we show that they carry the spectral imprint of convective driving. Observations from the Solar Dynamics Observatory and the Upgraded Coronal Multi-channel Polarimeter reveal the predicted spectrum of convectively driven waves in both weakly and rapidly expanding open fields, the likely sources of the fast and slow Alfvenic wind. Averaged over 270 intervals below the Alfven surface, the young wind sampled by Parker Solar Probe carries a similar spectrum. High-resolution spectroscopy from the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope resolves further spectral components that also appear in the wind. Convectively driven waves therefore supply a basal energy flux to the solar wind, alongside intermittent reconnection.

new.title: Optical Light-Curve Broadening in the Redback Binary PSR J2215+5135
new.summary: Spider millisecond pulsars offer a direct route to constrain neutron-star masses, including candidates above two solar masses, via optical light-curve modeling of the irradiated companion. This assumes stable irradiation. We report new $g'r'i'$ photometry of the redback PSR~J2215+5135 from the Iranian National Observatory in 2024 and compare it with the 2014 data of \citet{linares2018peering}. Peak brightness and orbital period are unchanged within uncertainties, but the light-curve wings are significantly broader in 2024, as the local deviations exceed $3\sigma$ on the rising branch in all filters, with an additional $i'$-band excess on the falling branch, giving a global permutation-test significance of $4.26\sigma$. A single-hot-spot model fits the 2024 data better than a spot-free one, but systematic residuals remain. The broader wings are reproduced only through correlated shifts in the spot, inclination, filling factor and companion temperature, which we regard as model compensation, not physics. An extended, variable heating component may also fit. The best-fit spot temperature differs between epochs by about $1060$\,K, comparable to its model dependence (about $900$\,K between two codes for 2014), so we do not interpret this as physical. Two epochs cannot show whether the change is gradual, sudden or short-lived. The inferred neutron-star mass depends on the spot treatment: $2.13^{+0.16}_{-0.13}\,M_\odot$ for 2014 with a hot spot, and $M_\mathrm{NS}=1.95^{+0.11}_{-0.07}\,M_\odot$ for 2024. These agree within about $1\sigma$, but come from differently shaped light curves, and the statistical uncertainties exclude heating-prescription systematics.

new.title: enCHASE: A pipeline for the calibration and analysis of CHASE/HIS observations
new.summary: We present 'enCHASE', an open-source pipeline for the calibration and analysis of H$\alpha$ and Fe I 6569 Å observations from the Chinese H$\alpha$ Solar Explorer (CHASE), addressing the lack of a public, documented tool for correcting residual instrumental effects in the mission's Level-1 data. The pipeline performs full-disk spatial registration, sub-field stabilization via correlation tracking and optical flow, wavelength offset correction, radiometric calibration against a high-resolution reference atlas, and stray-light correction. We demonstrate the method on six regions of different activity within one full-disk time series, including quiet Sun, a filament, a sunspot, a plage, a prominence, and an X1.2 flare. For reductions with both lines, we achieve a sub-pixel residual pointing error for tracked sub-fields, a wavelength zero-point that is stable to 1.2 mÅ (0.05 km\,s$^{-1}$), and an intensity calibration uncertainty of about 1\% of the continuum. When using only H$\alpha$, we reach slightly higher uncertainties and therefore recommend the use of both lines in the reduction.

new.title: Horizontal velocity eigenfunctions of solar inertial modes using local correlation tracking of magnetic features
new.summary: Solar inertial modes enable probes of the bulk of the convection zone over a broad latitude range. A proper study of high-latitude modes requires near-surface horizontal flow maps above 65 deg latitude at a cadence of at least one day. Previous observations have utilised ring-diagram analysis (RDA) of acoustic modes and local correlation tracking (LCT) of granules, but these methods do not have the capacity to access higher latitudes without compromising the signal-to-noise ratio (S/N). We measured flows associated with solar inertial modes using local correlation tracking of small magnetic features in SDO/HMI magnetograms separated by 1 h (LCTMag). This non-helioseismic method extracts horizontal near-surface flows with a good S/N up to 85 deg latitude. To carry out a comparison below 65 deg, we also measured flows using LCT of granulation features in continuum intensity images separated by 45 s (LCTGran). We constructed longitude-latitude maps of horizontal flows at a cadence of 6 h from LCTMag and LCTGran using overlapping 5 deg tiles. We additionally applied the RDA pipeline to HMI Dopplergrams over the same period to obtain flow maps at a cadence of 9 h. After removing large-scale systematics and long-term variations, we applied spectral analysis to identify modes in the inertial frequency range and extracted their spatial shapes via singular value decomposition. Mode shapes are consistent between LCTMag and LCTGran below 65 deg, but granulation tracking performs poorly at higher latitudes due to insufficient granule resolution. LCTMag provides higher-latitude access than both RDA and LCTGran with better S/N values, resulting in reduced spectral leakage from the window function. We also report a new retrograde inertial mode in the LCTMag dataset at frequency -192 nHz in the Carrington frame with a longitudinal wavenumber m = 3.

new.title: T-type brown dwarfs in Euclid DR1: from spectral classification to physical parameters
new.summary: The wide-area coverage and near-infrared spectroscopy of Euclid provide an opportunity to identify and characterize ultracool dwarfs. Its NISP slitless spectra cover prominent molecular absorption features of T-type brown dwarfs (T-BDs). We aim to identify T-BDs in Euclid DR1, determine their spectral types and atmospheric parameters, and estimate their masses, ages, radii, and distances. We select candidates using morphological criteria, near-infrared colour cuts, and spectral fitting, followed by visual inspection of multi-band images. Spectral types are determined using the SPLAT toolkit. Atmospheric parameters are derived independently using the Sonora Elf Owl and LOWZ model grids with Bayesian MCMC fitting. Evolutionary models are then used to estimate fundamental physical properties. We identify 141 T-BDs, including 134 newly identified objects. Effective temperature shows the best agreement between the two atmospheric models, with a mean absolute difference of 94 K, while other parameters exhibit larger discrepancies. The inferred mass-radius distribution shows decreasing radius with increasing mass, and older objects generally have smaller radii. We also identify 21 unusually blue T-BDs with I_E-H_E < 2.5. Their SEDs and colour overlap with previously reported white dwarf-brown dwarf (WD+BD) candidates suggest that some may be unresolved WD+T-BD systems. The two distance estimation methods show a mean absolute difference of approximately 37 pc. Three additional sources have nearby objects in Euclid images and are potential multiple-system candidates.

new.title: Investigating the Neupert Effect with HEL1OS/Aditya-L1
new.summary: We investigate the Neupert effect in solar flares using broadband hard X-ray observations from the HEL1OS instrument onboard Aditya-L1. By separating thermal and non-thermal components from HEL1OS spectrograms, we analyse a sample of 312 flares observed between November 2023 and May 2026. We find that the soft X-ray flux is strongly correlated with the time-integrated hard X-ray emission, with a median correlation coefficient of 0.984, indicating that Neupert-like behaviour is nearly ubiquitous in flares with detectable non-thermal emission. Extending beyond statistical correlation, we develop an empirical forward model in which the thermal lightcurve is reconstructed from the non-thermal emission by resolving the hard X-ray lightcurve into individual energy-release episodes and convolving their fitted profiles with finite thermal-response functions. This approach successfully reproduces the observed thermal evolution, including flares that exhibit quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs). Our results demonstrate that the broadband HEL1OS observations sample both thermal-dominated and non-thermal-dominated flare emission within a single instrument, providing an observation-driven link between the temporal structure of non-thermal HXR emission and the thermal X-ray response. This provides a different framework for interpreting flare energetics and temporal evolution using broadband hard X-ray measurements.

new.title: One, two, three, and a tilting frisbee: a transient state of some Be stars
new.summary: A recent reanalysis of the extreme variability of {\gamma} Cas in the 1930s/40s and 59 Cyg in the 1970s concluded that the disks of these two Be stars have each made a full turn over the poles (Baade+ 2023). For a better understanding of the underlying physics, more examples need to be identified, including less spectacular events, in which the disk was just tilted or warped. This paper discusses PZ Gem and HD 120678 as additional stars with spectroscopic evidence of a tilting disk: during extended line-emission periods intermittent shell phases occurred. In V1294 Aql, the symptoms of a tilting disk concerned H{\alpha} only. Three stars displayed heartbeat-like light variations. Unlike the original heartbeats resulting from distortions of red giant stars on an eccentric orbit, the much-larger-amplitude heartbeats in Be stars are due to changing orientations of the circumstellar disk. Two stars, Pleione and HD 120678, have exhibited both symptoms so that there is probably just one population of Be stars with tilting disks. The small number of candidates suggests that large-amplitude tilts/warpings of Be disks are not common. There is an extreme dominance of spectral types of B1 or earlier. In Be binaries resulting from previous mass transfer, spin-orbit misalignments and any torque on the Be disk should not be large. The necessary tilting force could be provided by a putative third star on an orbit highly inclined with respect to the inner binary (or just passing the B star) and be exerted either directly or indirectly via tilting the inner orbital plane. Beyond a refined knowledge of the multiplicity of Be stars, this would not promise much new insight into Be stars at large (except, perhaps, for some independent estimates of the viscosity parameter and a more 3D view of stellar winds). However, pruning the Be-star saga of such peculiarities may help reduce the level of confusion.

new.title: Determining the Spin-down of the White Dwarf in J191213.72-441045.1 using Optical Time-Series Photometry
new.summary: J191213.72-441045.1 (J1912-4410) is the second white dwarf pulsar to be discovered. These binary systems consist of a white dwarf primary with a cool companion and undergo pulsed emission from radio to X-ray wavelengths. The prototype of the class, AR Scorpii (AR Sco), exhibits a lack of accretion, which led to suggestions that the spin-down of the white dwarf is powering the system's non-thermal emission. However, J1912-4410 displays possible signatures of accretion, which allows for the possibility that its emission may operate via a different mechanism to AR Sco. To investigate this, we determined the first estimate for the spin period derivative of J1912-4410 from optical photometric data. This was carried out using ULTRACAM observations in multiple bandpasses spanning the last four years. Our estimate for the spin period derivative of 4.13(8)e-12 s/s is consistent across the u, g and r bandpasses of ULTRACAM. The corresponding spin-down power of 9^{+6}_{-5}e25 W is approximately equal to previous estimates for the system's bolometric luminosity. This suggests that the non-thermal emission of J1912-4410 is not solely powered by its spin-down, as near-perfect efficiency would be required. Additionally, our spin period derivative indicates that J1912-4410 is unlikely to be consistent with the synchronar model proposed to explain the emission of AR Sco, given previous upper limits for the white dwarf's magnetic field. Our findings imply that J1912-4410 has a distinct emission mechanism compared to AR Sco, which, if true, means that white dwarf pulsars are a heterogeneous class of binary systems.

new.title: NASA's Pandora SmallSat Mission: Gaussian Processes for Simulated Stellar Heterogeneity Corrections under Imperfect Stellar Models
new.summary: Stellar contamination is the primary bottleneck limiting robust atmospheric characterization of exoplanets orbiting active K- and M-dwarfs with James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) transmission spectroscopy. Launched in January 2026, NASA's Pandora SmallSat mission addresses this challenge through long-term, simultaneous visible photometry and near-infrared spectroscopy of planet-hosting stars, providing the data to disentangle planetary and stellar signals. However, conventional stellar-contamination corrections rely on stellar atmosphere models, making them vulnerable to model inaccuracies that can impede accurate inferences. Here, we investigate how Pandora data can be used to mitigate stellar contamination without an accurate host star model. We present a Gaussian-process-aided stellar retrieval framework that learns wavelength-dependent deviations from current stellar model grids. We propagate stellar contamination factors directly from the stellar retrieval into the planetary atmospheric retrievals, allowing the atmospheric inference to marginalize over stellar-contamination uncertainty without relying on a biased stellar model. Tests using simulated Pandora observations with realistic stellar model mismatch show that this framework consistently improves the recovery of disk-integrated stellar spectra. For a WASP-69 b-like system, this approach can reduce model-driven biases in inferred atmospheric properties, though degeneracies among stellar and atmospheric parameters can leave residual biases. This flexible, data-driven framework is a promising approach toward accurate stellar-contamination corrections and more robust atmospheric inference even when host-star model grids are inaccurate.

new.title: periapsis: A Comprehensive Orbital Fitting Package
new.summary: We introduce a new Python package \texttt{periapsis}, which computes posterior distributions for a variety of orbital parameters given astrometric and/or radial velocity data. \texttt{periapsis} not only returns posterior distributions, but also a variety of statistics assessing convergence and fit metrics as well as plotting capabilities for visualizing the orbital systems. In this paper, we describe our various methods for fitting Keplerian orbits to both astrometric and radial velocity data. We then show the breadth of binary systems that \texttt{periapsis} can characterize by comparing our computed parameters with known orbital systems. Finally, we discuss how \texttt{periapsis} will be a helpful tool for future data releases like \textit{Gaia} DR4 and \textit{Roman}.

cross.title: Flux and fluence effects on the Vacuum-UV photodesorption and photoprocessing of CO$_2$ ices
cross.summary: CO$_2$ is a major component of the icy mantles surrounding dust grains in planet and star formation regions. Understanding its photodesorption is crucial for explaining gas phase abundances in the coldest environments of the interstellar medium irradiated by vacuum-UV (VUV) photons. Photodesorption yields determined experimentally from CO$_2$ samples grown at low temperatures (T=15~K) have been found to be very sensitive to experimental methods and conditions. Several mechanisms have been suggested for explaining the desorption of CO$_2$, O$_2$ and CO from CO$_2$ ices. In the present study, the cross sections characterizing the dynamics of photodesorption as a function of photon fluence (determined from released molecules in the gas phase) and of ice composition modification (determined in situ in the solid phase) are compared for the first time for different photon flux conditions (from 7.3$\times 10^{12}$~photon/s/cm$^2$ to 2.2$\times 10^{14}$~photon/s/cm$^2$) using monochromatic synchrotron radiation in the VUV range (on the DESIRS beamline at SOLEIL). This approach reveals that CO and O$_2$ desorption are decorrelated from that of CO$_2$. CO and O$_2$ photodesorption yields depend on photon flux conditions and can be linked to surface chemistry. By contrast, the phodesorption yield of CO$_2$ is independent of the photon flux conditions and can be linked to bulk ice chemical modification, consistently with an indirect desorption induced by electronic transition (DIET) process.

cross.title: Stellar Obliquities of Cold Jupiter and Brown Dwarf Systems I: Spin-Orbit Misalignment Grows with Orbital Eccentricity
cross.summary: Stellar obliquity provides insights into the formation and dynamical evolution of planetary systems. Most obliquity measurements to date have focused on close-in transiting giant planets, whose orbits may have been altered by migration and tidal interactions. In contrast, the stellar obliquities of cold Jupiters, the most common class of giant planets, remain largely unexplored. Here, we measure the minimum stellar obliquity for 69 cold Jupiters and brown dwarfs (M_p > 0.3 M_J, a > 1 au), by comparing stellar inclinations derived from stellar rotation measurements with companion orbital inclinations constrained by radial velocities, relative astrometry and Hipparcos-Gaia absolute astrometry. We find that spin-orbit misalignments are common among cold Jupiters and brown dwarf companions, with 19/69 (28 +6/-5%) exhibiting significant misalignments. Furthermore, the stellar obliquities depends strongly on orbital eccentricity, whereby 0/17 (0 +8/-0%) companions with e_orb <= 0.15 are misaligned, compared to 19/52 (37 +7/-6%) with more eccentric orbits. This pattern reveals a connection between orbital eccentricity and stellar obliquity: companions on nearly circular orbits tend to be aligned with their host stars, whereas those on eccentric orbits exhibit a broader range of obliquities. This finding suggests that post-formation dynamical interactions, such as planet-planet scattering or secular chaos, may play an important role in exciting both orbital eccentricities and spin-orbit misalignments.

cross.title: Over a Half-decade Study of Crab Giant Pulses Observed with I-LOFAR
cross.summary: This work details the analysis of 1,048,138 single pulses from the Crab pulsar detected with the Irish LOFAR station over a 6-year observation campaign spanning 154 epochs and 347.9 hours at 110-190 MHz. Of the detections in the sample 550,445 are giant pulses (GPs, with S/N $\geq$ 10), making it the largest analysed sample to date. The power law indices for the S/N, flux density and fluence distributions range from 3.0-3.4 for the main pulse population and 3.3-3.5 for the inter-pulse population. A subset of 5,474 GPs (with S/N $\geq$ 100) were used to model scattering across the observing band to investigate the entanglement of dispersion measure (DM) and scattering. It was found that DM and scattering have a strong correlation coefficient of 0.70-0.71 across the entire campaign. Removing the long-term trend using a running median windowed at 125-190 days lowers the correlation to 0.48-0.50 respectively. The implications of these DM and scattering observations from the perspective of both the Crab Nebula's structure and the solar wind are discussed, including a rise in DM from August to October 2024 indicating AU-scale density variation consistent with fine substructure within Rayleigh-Taylor shaped filamentary ejecta.

cross.title: Moon Radio Interferometer for Science and Exploration (MoonRISE): A Mission Concept for a Low-Frequency Radio Interferometer on the Lunar Farside
cross.summary: The universe below 20 MHz remains one of space science's last unexplored frontiers, inaccessible from Earth due to its ionosphere and terrestrial radio frequency interference (RFI). We present the mission concept for the Moon Radio Interferometer for Science and Exploration (MoonRISE), an all-sky imaging, low-frequency radio telescope operating from 100 kHz-30 MHz from the lunar farside, the quietest radio environment in the inner Solar System. If realized, MoonRISE would be the first radio interferometer on the Moon and the first connected-element radio interferometer in space. Its science objectives are to (1) determine how solar wind turbulence drives plasma heating, acceleration, and space weather evolution in the inner heliosphere, by measuring the scattering of type III solar radio bursts between 2-20 solar radii; (2) constrain the density, structure, and variability of the lunar ionosphere and its effects on surface communication; and (3) resolve the plasma sources and magnetospheric dynamics that power Uranian Kilometric Radiation, observable for the first time since Voyager 2 in 1986. The same observations would yield all-sky maps of the low-frequency sky, subsurface structure at the landing site, and a characterization of the farside RF environment. The Radio Interferometer concept consists of nine 3.5 m dipoles embedded in a 1.5 km optical-fiber tether deployed by a rover, with power- and RF-over-fiber enabling RFI-free mapping. A rover-mounted Ground Penetrating Radar (300-2000 MHz) would measure regolith dielectric properties and bedrock depth to characterize the dipoles' RF performance. We describe the science objectives, a reference landing site in Lacus Luxuriae, a notional concept of operations, and the payload design and technology maturity. The concept builds on SunRISE and OVRO-LWA heritage and could serve as a basis for a future selected mission.

cross.title: Planetary Habitable Zones around Magnetized White Dwarfs
cross.summary: White dwarfs are known to host remnant planetary material, indicating that rocky objects can survive post-main-sequence evolution and migrate into very close orbits. However, the decline of white dwarf luminosity makes it difficult for a planet to remain habitable for long when relying only on the white dwarf's irradiative heating. While several non-radiative energy sources have been proposed, the role of white dwarf magnetism in planetary energy budgets remains largely unexplored. We examine whether magnetic unipolar induction could provide sustained heating for close-in rocky planets. By coupling white dwarf cooling tracks with an orbit-dependent induction model, we evaluate the contribution of ohmic dissipation to planetary surface energy budgets and estimate the upper limit with efficient heat deposition. It is possible for the induction heating to supply a nearly steady surface energy flux for certain orbital distances and stellar spins, partially offsetting the decline in the white dwarf irradiation at late times. This leads to a persistent outer temperate region and, in some cases, a narrow inner zone that emerges after substantial cooling, identifying magnetic induction as a viable long-lived supplement to radiative heating.

cross.title: Uphill Diffusion in Yukawa Plasmas
cross.summary: In a fluid mixture of many species an individual species can diffuse toward higher concentration without any external driving force because its flux is coupled to the gradients of other components. Such `uphill diffusion' is well known in the chemical and metallurgy literature but to our knowledge has not been studied for strongly coupled plasmas in neutron star and white dwarf interiors. We have previously developed a semi-analytic diffusion model that accurately predicts diffusion coefficients of individual species in a mixture in equilibrium. Uphill diffusion allows us to test this model out of equilibrium, and also test a generalized Darken relation for predicting diffusivities. We derive an analytic theory and compare to three-component molecular dynamics simulations and find very good agreement. This provides a novel out-of-equilibrium test of the generalization of our diffusion model to arbitrary multi-component mixtures.

cross.title: Discovery of Trailing Spiral Dust Alignment in the Dust Polarization of HL Tau at $λ= 2.1$ mm
cross.summary: Polarimetric observations of protoplanetary disks at (sub)millimeter wavelengths constrain dust grain properties, dynamics, and alignment mechanisms. We present new high-resolution ALMA Band 4 (2.1 mm) polarization observations of HL Tau with spatial resolutions of $\sim$0.08$''$ (11.78 au) and $\sim$0.19$''$ (27.99 au). Linearly decomposing the polarization into contributions from dust scattering and thermal emission by aligned grains, we analyze the new Band 4 data and published high-resolution Band 7 (870 $\mu$m) observations. Thermal emission from aligned grains dominates the polarization across the disk at Band 4, in contrast to the scattering-dominated Band 7, and both mechanisms vary radially with the disk substructures, consistent with expected optical depth variations. At Band 4, we detect a coherent angular deviation from purely azimuthal grain alignment, in which the streamlines of the alignment field yield trailing spirals with respect to disk rotation. A single global offset angle quantifies this deviation as $2.83^\circ\pm0.33^\circ$ and $4.10^\circ\pm0.09^\circ$ (statistical uncertainties) from two robust weightings, and the detection reaches a significance of $\approx7\sigma$ under conservative uncertainty estimates. This trailing orientation is consistent with aerodynamic ("badminton birdie-like") alignment driven by gas-dust drift near pressure bumps. However, under an axisymmetric disk velocity structure, this interpretation requires Stokes numbers two to three orders of magnitude larger than expected for the grains dominating the millimeter emission. At Band 7, the polarization angle is weakly sensitive to the alignment direction and exhibits a near/far-side antisymmetric structure that the model cannot reproduce. The Band 7 data therefore neither support nor contradict the Band 4 result.

cross.title: The Splash population confined to the Milky Way bar region
cross.summary: We investigate the chemo-dynamical properties of in-situ stars in the Galactic bar region (central $5$ kpc), specifically the inner Galactic counterpart of the solar-neighbourhood Splash population (in situ halo). We use a sample of APOGEE DR17 red giants with Gaia astrometry and AstroNN distances, and separate bulge/bar stellar populations dynamically using a normalised time-averaged bar-frame angular momentum, $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}$. Chemo-dynamical maps in the $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}$-[Fe/H] plane reveal a pronounced extension of the bar population towards $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}<0$ (non-bar-following orbits) within $-1.0<{\rm [Fe/H]}<-0.3$, characterised by high eccentricities, large $z_{\rm max}$ and an extended spheroidal orbit density distribution, and accounting for $\sim 30\%$ of all stars at these metallicities. These $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}<0$ stars have [Mg/Fe] and [Al/Fe] abundances similar to those of stars on ${\rm x_1}$ orbits at the same [Fe/H], and they match the solar-neighbourhood Splash in its metallicity and abundance ratio distributions. We therefore refer to them as the $\textit{central Splash}$. The presence of a significant central Splash underscores the role of the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus merger in the early history of the Galaxy. We find a similar, weaker extension in the $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}$-[Fe/H] maps for extremely metal-rich stars, which are confined to the bulge. At metallicities [Fe/H] $<0.3$, we find no additional classical bulge population in these maps beyond the central Splash and proto-Galactic populations $-$ the high-$\alpha$ bulge appears to have evolved from the early high-$\alpha$ disc.

repl.title: JWST Observations of SN 2024ggi II: NIRSpec Spectroscopy and CO Modeling at 285 and 385 Days Past the Explosion
repl.summary: We present James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) NIRSpec observations of SN~2024ggi, spanning wavelengths of 1.7--5.5 micron at +285.51 and +385.27 days post-explosion. These nebular spectra are dominated by asymmetric emission lines from atomic species including H, Ca, Ar, C, Mg, Ni, Co, and Fe, indicative of an aspherical explosion. The other strong features are molecular CO vibrational bands from the fundamental and first overtone. We introduce a novel, data-driven approach using non-LTE 3D radiative transfer simulations to model the CO emission with high fidelity. This method enables us to constrain the three-dimensional CO distribution and its radial temperature structure. CO formation is found to occur prior to day +285, with subsequent evolution characterized by progressive evaporation. The CO mass decreases from approximately (7.9 to 1.0)e-4 Msol, while the average temperature drops from about 2300 K to 1800 K. Concurrently, the CO distribution becomes increasingly clumped (f_c = 5.5 to 10). The minimum velocity of the CO-emitting region decreases (v1=1400 to 800 km/s), above the receding photosphere velocity (vph=500 km/s), suggesting the photosphere resides within Si-rich layers. However, the temperature profile indicates that only a narrow zone reaches the conditions necessary for SiO formation. Due to a lack of observational constraints, SiO clumping is not modeled, and thus, synthetic SiO profiles for mass estimates are not highlighted. We discuss the implications of these findings for dust formation processes in SN2024ggi.

repl.title: Astronomical Cardiology II: A Search For Heartbeat Stars Using APOGEE and TESS
repl.summary: Stellar binaries in short-period, highly eccentric systems with significant tidal deformations near pericenter, also known as heartbeat stars, are a laboratory for studying dynamical tides and oscillations in stars. We identify 50 heartbeat stars using TESS light curves of stars identified as binaries using SDSS APOGEE. We fit their phase-folded TESS light curves with an analytic model to measure their orbital periods, eccentricities, inclinations, and arguments of periastron. We measure the mass function of targets with enough APOGEE radial velocity observations to obtain a constraint on the secondary mass. We confirm our previous results that the non-giant heartbeat stars have started to evolve off the main sequence and that the fraction of (near) main sequence binaries that are heartbeat stars rises rapidly with effective temperature.

repl.title: The quiescent states of V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr: VLT/X-shooter and Swift/XRT+UVOT observations
repl.summary: Symbiotic recurrent novae are symbiotic binaries in which multiple thermonuclear outbursts have been observed. Only four such systems are currently known in the Galaxy: T CrB, RS Oph, V745 Sco, and V3890 Sgr. They provide convenient laboratories for studying accretion and binary interaction in symbiotic novae during quiescence. We characterise the quiescent states of the less-studied systems V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr and compare their properties with those of T CrB and RS Oph. We analyse VLT/X-shooter spectra together with Swift/XRT and UVOT observations, supplemented by ground-based optical photometry and archival data. We determine the spectral types of the red-giant donors and compare the spectral energy distributions of the systems with those of single bulge giants of the same spectral type to investigate the properties of the accretion. We classify the donor stars in V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr as M7III and M6.5III, respectively. We derive reddenings and distances by comparing the systems' colours and magnitudes with those of typical giants in the Galactic bulge. Both objects exhibit a significant ultraviolet excess relative to normal late-type giants, indicating ongoing accretion during quiescence. From this excess we calculate lower limits on the mass transfer rate in the systems to be $\dot{M}_\mathrm{acc}\gtrsim2.4\times10^{-8}\ M_\odot\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and $\dot{M}_\mathrm{acc}\gtrsim2.5\times10^{-8}\ M_\odot\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ for V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr, respectively. We discuss several evolutionary scenarios for the quiescent state in the systems, which are consistent with such high lower limits of the mass transfer rate.

repl.title: The Role of Preceding CMEs and SIRs in Enhancing Shock Acceleration of Electrons
repl.summary: The role of large-scale pre-existing interplanetary structures, including preceding coronal mass ejections (CMEs) and stream interaction regions (SIRs), in shaping the shock acceleration environment for energetic electrons remains not fully understood. In this study, we investigate nine interplanetary shocks observed by the Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory (STEREO) that are associated with significant MeV electron enhancements, as such enhancements are rarely observed at interplanetary shocks. We combine remote-sensing observations, drag-based modeling, and in-situ measurements to analyze the shock propagation through pre-existing interplanetary structures. Eight of the nine events are associated with a preceding slow or intermediate-speed CME, while six shocks are in-situ observed propagating within preceding ICMEs, indicating that large-scale upstream trapping structures are a common feature of these events. Further analysis identifies three distinct scenarios associated with enhanced electron acceleration: shocks propagating through preceding ICMEs, shock-SIR interactions, and direct injection of flare-accelerated electrons into SIRs. As a representative shock-in-ICME event, the 2012 January 29 low-$\beta$, quasi-perpendicular shock ($\theta_{Bn}\sim87^\circ$) is further investigated using observations together with one-dimensional Monte Carlo test-particle simulations of a shock propagating into a large-scale upstream magnetic loop. The simulation suggests that the upstream loop prolongs electron residence near the shock and substantially enhances acceleration efficiency. These results demonstrate that large-scale interplanetary structures can precondition the upstream magnetic environment, providing favorable conditions for prolonged electron residence and efficient shock acceleration.

repl.title: The long period radio transient ASKAP J1448-68 is a cataclysmic variable
repl.summary: Wide-field time-domain radio surveys have recently unveiled a new class of Galactic radio emitter: long period radio transients (LPTs). Despite the rapid pace of discovery, their origins remain poorly understood, with two main theories emerging: slowly spinning magnetars or binary white dwarfs (WDs) with magnetic interactions. All three LPTs with well-characterised optical counterparts are WDs in binary systems, but even within that class there is diversity, with one accreting and two detached systems. In this Letter, we show that the LPT ASKAP J1448-68 is a cataclysmic variable (CV)---a WD accreting from a low-mass companion---with a spectroscopic orbital period consistent with the radio pulse period, and specifically, potentially consistent with being a polar. Unlike the other known LPT CV, ASKAP J1448-68 does not exhibit the He II emission that is a hallmark of magnetic CVs in their high accretion states. We also present new optical time-series and infrared photometric observations, showing flickering at the 10% level and suggesting a possible period bouncer origin. This identification of ASKAP J1448-68 adds to the small sample of characterised LPT counterparts, and shows that LPT emission can persist in an accreting WD binary at a low accretion rate.

repl.title: Flare driven habitability: Expanding life's potential around low-mass stars
repl.summary: The traditional definition of the circumstellar habitable zone (HZ) focuses on liquid water, but neglects the crucial role of ultraviolet (UV) radiation in prebiotic chemistry. Low-mass stars typically emit insufficient UV radiation for photochemistry throughout the liquid water HZs during quiescent states. However, frequent flares can provide substantial UV fluxes, potentially fostering habitable conditions. We refine the concept of a UV habitable zone (UV-HZ) by incorporating a temperature-dependent model for RNA precursor synthesis. Furthermore, we explore a parameterized spectral energy distribution model and adopt an empirical flare frequency distribution for flares on different stars to quantify their UV contribution. Applying this framework to different flaring stars, we find the UV-HZ around low-mass stars can extend to inner regions, and overlap with the traditional HZ in wide ranges. Apply the analysis to 9 planets around Kepler flaring stars, three planets are located within both the refined UV-HZ and liquid water habitable zone (LW-HZ) without causing ozone depletion. Our findings highlight the significant role of flares in expanding the potential for life around low-mass stars, offering a revised perspective on exoplanet habitability criteria.

repl.title: Combining the Mass--Radius Posteriors of PSR J0030+0451 Allowing for Unknown Correlations and Model Systematics
repl.summary: The NASA Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer (\emph{NICER}) mission measures the X-ray pulse profiles of millisecond pulsars and uses pulse profile modeling (PPM) techniques to constrain their masses ($M$) and radii ($R$), in order to probe the state of matter in their interiors. One of the most studied pulsars, PSR J0030+0451, has been analyzed by multiple groups using different choices of hotspot models. The different choices of hotspot prescriptions to fit the same observational data led to different $M$--$R$ posteriors that do not completely agree with one another, resulting in a practical bottleneck for dense-matter equation-of-state (EoS) inference. In this paper, we adapt a Bayesian combination framework to the published $M$--$R$ posteriors of PSR J0030+0451 while allowing for unknown correlations and systematic uncertainties. Using this technique, we combine eight existing $M$--$R$ posteriors into a single estimate of the source parameters. The resulting constraint is $M=1.53^{+0.31}_{-0.27}\,M_\odot$, $R=13.44^{+2.95}_{-2.38}\,\mathrm{km}$, and compactness $C=0.169^{+0.018}_{-0.021}$ (68\% credible intervals). The combined distribution retains the lower- and higher-mass solutions obtained with different hotspot models. Conditional interpolation with PSR~J0437--4715 gives $R_{1.4}=11.84^{+0.88}_{-0.83}\,\mathrm{km}$. Our results provide a combined $M$--$R$ constraint for J0030+0451 that accounts for shared observations and cross-model uncertainty, and a framework for combining correlated measurements of the same source.

repl.title: Interstellar Complex Organic Molecules and Molecular Outflows in NGC 1333 IRAS 4B and 4B' Observed Using NOEMA
repl.summary: We present interferometric observations with the Northern Extended Millimeter Array (NOEMA) of NGC 1333 IRAS 4B and 4B', two young stellar objects (YSOs) within the Perseus molecular cloud. YSOs, especially Class 0 protostars, are rich in gas-phase interstellar complex organic molecules (iCOMs), but relatively little is known about the spatial distribution of these important prebiotic molecules. Various molecules were imaged within IRAS 4B and the surrounding area in the 145 GHz spectral range, revealing hundreds of molecular transitions within the warm inner envelope of IRAS 4B. This work provides derived physical parameters (rotational temperature, column density, velocity shift with respect to local standard of rest, and full-width at half-maximum spectral line width) for 11 molecules toward IRAS 4B including methanol (CH$_3$OH and isotopologues), methyl formate (HCOOCH$_3$), dimethyl ether (CH$_3$OCH$_3$), acetaldehyde (CH$_3$CHO), ethanol (C$_2$H$_5$OH), glycolaldehyde (CH$_2$OHCHO), acetone (CH$_3$COCH$_3$), and isocyanic acid (HNCO). Out of these molecules, 10 are iCOMs (excluding HNCO) that trace the inner envelope of IRAS 4B and mark it as a rich source of organic material. There is a strong spatial correlation between the continuum emission of IRAS 4B and iCOM molecular emission and among various iCOMs with each other. Physical parameter and integrated intensity maps show that IRAS 4B is a binary protostar system that drives a jet in a north-south orientation and an outflow in a northwest-southeast orientation. IRAS 4B' also drives a west-east outflow but shows no evidence of molecular emission cospatial with its continuum emission.
